correctness.rationale: Residue-class adjacency gives the exact parity-dependent fiber structure. Twin classes imply at most one white per fiber. With at least three white fibers every blue vertex has at least two white neighbors, while every two-fiber profile has an explicit forcing sequence, so Z=N-2 and the three-term polynomial follows. The coefficient inversion recovers q and s exactly. Explicit bilinear constructions give real ranks 2 or 3; rank 2 is impossible for even q>=4 because s>=q>=4 and a two-dimensional nondegenerate real symmetric form has at most two isotropic lines available for multipartite parts.

value.rationale: The result completely enumerates standard zero forcing sets at the minimum boundary for every finite local nonfield unit graph, makes the polynomial explicitly invertible to the residue-field and maximal-ideal sizes, and identifies the exact arithmetic regime in which maximum nullity drops one below zero forcing. This contrast between a parity-independent forcing polynomial and a parity-sensitive real rank is a natural structural boundary, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
